problem.title: Fill the Divisor Grid
problem.statement: Every divisor of 72 = 2³ × 3² has the form 2ᵃ3ᵇ. How many divisors are formed when 0 ≤ a ≤ 3 and 0 ≤ b ≤ 2?
hints: Count the allowed values of a and b, including zero.
Pair each a-choice with every b-choice.

solutionSteps.title: Count each range
solutionSteps.body: There are four choices for a and three for b.

solutionSteps.title: Combine independent choices
solutionSteps.body: Every a pairs with every b, so 4 × 3 = 12 divisors.

notes: The exponent grid has exactly twelve unique cells.

problem.title: Count the Divisors of 180
problem.statement: How many positive divisors does 180 have?

solutionSteps.title: Multiply exponent choices
solutionSteps.body: The exponent ranges have 3, 3, and 2 choices, so (2+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 18.

validationMethods: independent factor-pair enumeration producing nine pairs
notes: Nine factor pairs give eighteen distinct divisors because 180 is not a square.

problem.title: Divisors Along One Prime Axis
problem.statement: How many positive divisors does 64 = 2⁶ have?

solutionSteps.title: Count exponent choices
solutionSteps.body: The divisors are 2ᵃ for a = 0,1,2,3,4,5,6, giving seven choices.

validationMethods: inclusive exponent count from zero through six

problem.title: Divisors That Contain Twelve
problem.statement: How many positive divisors of 360 are divisible by 12?

solutionSteps.title: Restrict the exponents
solutionSteps.body: The 2-exponent has 2 choices, the 3-exponent has 2 choices, and the 5-exponent has 2 choices.

notes: Exactly eight divisors contain the required prime sub-inventory.

problem.title: Odd Divisors of 840
problem.statement: How many positive divisors of 840 are odd?
hints: An odd divisor uses no factors of 2.

solutionSteps.title: Fix the 2-exponent
solutionSteps.body: Set the exponent of 2 to zero. Each of 3, 5, and 7 has exponent 0 or 1.

validationMethods: independent observation that odd divisors are exactly divisors of 105, which has eight divisors
notes: Removing the factor 2 leaves the squarefree odd part 105.

problem.title: Count the Square Divisors
problem.statement: How many positive divisors of 2⁵ × 3³ × 5² are perfect squares?
hints: A square has even prime exponents.
Count the allowed even exponents in each range.

solutionSteps.title: List allowed exponent sets
solutionSteps.body: For 2 use {0,2,4}; for 3 use {0,2}; for 5 use {0,2}.

validationMethods: independent bijection with divisors of 2 squared times 3 times 5 after halving exponents, yielding twelve
notes: Every even-exponent tuple produces one distinct square divisor.
